correctness.rationale: For n>=2 the process is uniform among currently feasible edges because independent random priorities are exchangeable conditional on the past. At k unmatched labels on each side and overlap r the feasible count is k^2-r, with transitions r->r-2,r-1,r in weights r(r-1),2r(k-r),(k-r)^2. At k>=2 there is always a feasible edge; failure iff final shared singleton. The conditional first-moment identity telescopes to the exact nonnegative defect 2/(n+1)-Q_n=4 sum_{k=2}^n E[(R_k)_2/(k(k-1)(k+1)(k^2-R_k))]. The second-factorial contraction gives E[(R_k)_2]<=k^4/n^2; hence the specified 16 H_n/n^2 bound and n Q_n->2 without extrapolation. Independent exact bit-mask DP agrees with overlap-chain probabilities through n=7; Q_2=0,Q_3=1/3,Q_4=4/21. The polynomial contraction inequality is positive at k=2 and increasing thereafter. I found no missing boundary assumption.
